title: Paranormal investigations coming to Maple Ridge's Haney House
excerpt: Cornerstone Supernatural hosts The Dead of Night museum fundraiser in October
content:
Published 5:45 pm Monday, September 21, 2026

As the Halloween season looms, the Maple Ridge Museum and Cornerstone Supernatural are once again hosting paranormal investigations at the historic Haney House.

The event billed “The Dead of Night” is happening on Oct. 2 and 3, and members of the public can take part in what organizers call “an eerie evening of fun.”

The professional paranormal investigation team will lead 75-minute guided tours exploring the darker side of Haney House’s history. Those attending are invited to learn about the tools and techniques paranormal investigators use, and even try them out, as they search for signs of the spirits said to linger within the walls of this historic home.

Maple Ridge Historical Society executive director Gordana Dimovska said this has been a popular event for the museum in recent years, as people look for spirits in a house that was inhabited by the Haney family for many years. Two people are known to have passed away at the house. Although it is not known specifically as a haunted house, it has a unique character from times gone by.

“It’s an old house… a lot of people feel like they can sense an energy there,” Dimovska said.

She said the historic house is unique in that almost everything there once belonged to the Haney family, and was donated to the museum society.

Cornerstone Supernatural is a Vancouver-based group of paranormal enthusiasts, and they have done numerous investigations at historic locations and places where there are reports of unusual activity.

This fun event is the biggest fundraising event of the year for the museum, said Dimovska, and the funds raised will be used to maintain Haney House and for other costs for the non-profit society.

Tours begin at 6 p.m., with a new tour starting every 20 minutes. The last tour begins at 8 p.m.
